questions.stem: What is usually the main objective of a brand new business?
options: Survival
Profit maximisation
Market share
Employee welfare
questions.why: Everything else requires still existing. In practice survival means managing cash, because a business with profit on paper fails if it cannot pay wages this month.
whyNot: Maximum profit is rarely achievable in year one and is not the priority.
Share matters once established.
Important, and it comes after the business is secure.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best definition of sales maximisation?
options: Selling the greatest possible volume or value, even where it is not the most profitable option
Making the largest possible profit
Producing at the lowest possible cost per unit
Holding the largest share of a market
questions.why: Sales maximisation targets volume. It can build presence and scale, and high volume at a thin margin can produce less profit than lower volume at a better one.
whyNot: That is profit maximisation, which is a different target.
That is cost efficiency.
That is a market share objective.

questions.stem: Why is survival about cash rather than profit?
options: A profitable business still fails if it cannot pay its bills when they fall due
Profit is never important to a new business
Cash and profit are the same thing
Survival requires no money at all
questions.why: Profit is calculated over a period and includes sales not yet paid for. Cash is what actually leaves the bank to pay wages and suppliers, so insolvency is a cash event.
whyNot: Profit matters, particularly to lenders, but it is not what stops the business closing this month.
They are different, and the distinction is directly examinable.
Survival is entirely about being able to meet obligations.

questions.stem: Which objective most directly conflicts with employee welfare?
options: Cost efficiency
Customer satisfaction
Survival
Social objectives
questions.why: Better pay, conditions and training all raise costs, which works against producing at the lowest possible cost per unit.
whyNot: Well-treated staff usually deliver better service, so these two often support each other.
In a crisis they conflict, but cost efficiency is the direct and permanent tension.
Social objectives and employee welfare usually point the same way.

questions.stem: A business discounts heavily to increase its market share. What is the trade-off?
options: Share is bought at the cost of margin now, for a benefit that may not arrive
Share and profit always rise together
There is no cost to discounting
Market share cannot be increased by discounting
questions.why: Every discounted unit earns less. The justification is that share brings supplier power, retailer strength and the ability to raise prices later, and that later benefit is not guaranteed.
whyNot: Discounting for share usually lowers profit in the short run.
Discounting directly reduces the margin on every unit.
It is one of the most common ways to buy share.

questions.stem: Why do business objectives change over time?
options: The priorities of a start-up, a growing business and a mature business are different
Objectives must legally be changed every year
Owners become bored with their objectives
Objectives never change in practice
questions.why: Survival at start-up, growth and share in the growth phase, profit and efficiency in maturity, and survival again in a downturn. If a question tells you the stage, use it.
whyNot: There is no such requirement.
The change is driven by the situation, not boredom.
They change frequently, and examiners reward noticing it.

questions.stem: Which of the following makes an objective useful?
options: It is measurable and has a deadline
It is ambitious and vaguely worded
It is agreed by all stakeholders
It is kept confidential
questions.why: Without a measure and a date you cannot tell whether you achieved it. Raising an average review score from 4.1 to 4.5 within twelve months can be judged; improving customer satisfaction cannot.
whyNot: Vagueness is the problem, because it makes success untestable.
Desirable but not what makes it a usable objective, and stakeholders often disagree.
Confidentiality has no bearing on whether it is a good objective.

questions.stem: Why can short-run profit maximisation damage long-run profit?
options: Actions that raise profit now, such as cutting quality or training, reduce competitiveness later
Profit is always higher in the short run
Long-run profit cannot be measured
Maximising profit is illegal
questions.why: Cutting quality raises this year's margin and loses next year's customers; cutting training raises profit now and productivity falls later. The time frame is one of the most reliable evaluation angles on any objectives question.
whyNot: No general rule. It depends entirely on the decisions taken.
It is measured continuously; it is simply harder to forecast.
Perfectly legal.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best definition of cost efficiency as an objective?
options: Producing at the lowest possible cost per unit
Selling at the lowest possible price
Having the lowest total costs of any business
Spending as little as possible on marketing
questions.why: Cost efficiency is about unit cost. It enables competitive pricing and protects profit in a price-led market, and pushed too far it cuts quality.
whyNot: That is a pricing decision, which low unit costs make possible.
Total costs depend on size. A large efficient firm has higher total costs than a small inefficient one.
Marketing is one cost among many, and cutting it is not the same as being efficient.

questions.stem: A guesthouse discounts rooms to win reviews and improve its platform ranking. Which objectives is it balancing?
options: Market share and customer satisfaction now, against profit now
Cost efficiency against employee welfare
Survival against social objectives
Sales maximisation against independence
questions.why: Discounting sacrifices margin to build ranking and review score, both of which bring future bookings. Whether that trade is worth it is precisely what a 10-mark question is asking.
whyNot: Nothing here concerns unit costs or staff conditions.
No social objective is described.
Independence is a personal motive and is not in tension here.
